text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Centre Union MP Romualdas Ozolas drew up a draft law to et up a national investigation bureau to fight fraud in banks and confirmed that he would agree to head the institution.
- Centre Union candidate Danute Aleksiuniene won the run off elections to Lithuania's parliament in Trakai district.

- Oil products refined in Mazheikiai Nafta have started to become accepted on the local market. Starting from last year, Western oil companies started to trade with petroleum produced in Mazheikiu Nafta although earlier they said they were importing all the petroleum from Scandinavia.
- Lithuanian Gas, one of the blue chips on the Vilnius bourse, said its losses in 1996 were 77.6 million litas.
- The newspaper has an exclusive interview with French actress Annie Girardot who will perform in Vilnius tonight.
- "We are standing on the doorstep to NATO," said parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis after meetings with high-ranking U.S. officials during a trip to Washington.
- Kuro Aparatura reported a net profit of over 15 million litas in 1996 but the company faces difficulties paying salaries because of more than 50 million litas of debts by consumers.
- Neste has invested around $19 million since 1991 in Lithuania and sells an average 800,000 tonnes of oil products a year. The company expects to get its first profit in the country in 2000.
- Master Foods Lithuania produced 5,000 tonnes of cat and dogs food in Klaipeda in 1996 and wants to double production.
- Market experts do not forecast a big price leap after the increase of excise duties of 43-58 percent on fuel.
- French banking giant Societe Generale met central bank officials lat week to investigate the possibility of opening a branch office in Lithuania.
